title: Dinar of Mahmud
creator: Unknown mint; present-day Afghanistan
caption: A gold dinar bearing the name of Mahmud, dated 419 AH / 1028 CE. The museum catalogues it among its Islamic coins.

title: Nomisma with Constantine IX Monomachus
creator: Byzantium
caption: A Byzantine gold nomisma associated with Constantine IX Monomachus. The museum dates this coin to his reign, 1042–1055.

title: Dinar of Tughril
creator: Nishapur, Iran
caption: A gold dinar of Tughril, dated 444 AH / 1052–53 CE. The museum identifies its place of production as Nishapur.
sourceNote: Museum catalogue title: Dinar of Tughril (r. 1040–63)

title: Dirham with a Double-Headed Bird of Prey
creator: Hisn Kayfa, present-day Turkey
caption: This copper dirham of Nasir al-Din Mahmud carries a double-headed bird of prey. It is dated 615 AH / 1218–19 CE.
sourceNote: Museum catalogue title: Dirham of Nasir al-Din Mahmud (r. 1201–22): Double-Headed Bird of Prey

title: Dirham with the Sun and Lion
creator: Konya, present-day Turkey
caption: A silver dirham of Ghiyath al-Din Kai Khusrau II, with the sun-and-lion device named in the museum record. It is dated 638 AH / 1240–41 CE.
sourceNote: Museum catalogue title: Dirham of Ghiyath al-Din Kai Khusrau II (r. 1239–46); Astrological Device (Sun-Lion)

title: Mouton d'Or of Jean le Bon
creator: France
caption: A gold coin from the reign of King Jean le Bon of France. The museum dates this Gothic-period example to 1350–1364.
sourceNote: Museum catalogue title: Mouton d'Or of King Jean le Bon of France, 1350-1364

title: Noble of Edward III
creator: England
caption: Edward III stands in a ship on one face; an ornamental cross appears on the other. The noble was the first English gold coin struck in substantial numbers.
sourceNote: Museum catalogue title: Noble: Edward III Standing in Ship with Shield of Arms (obverse); Ornamental Cross with Lis Terminals (reverse)

title: Halfcrown of Elizabeth I
creator: England
caption: This gold halfcrown pairs a portrait of Elizabeth I with a crowned shield of arms. The museum dates it to 1560–61.
sourceNote: Museum catalogue title: Halfcrown: Elizabeth I (obverse); Crowned Shield of Arms (reverse)

title: Coin with Gemini Zodiac Sign
creator: India
caption: A silver coin from India bearing the zodiac sign Gemini. The museum dates it to 1027 AH / 1618 CE.

title: Coin with Sign of Libra
creator: Agra, India
caption: A gold coin bearing the sign of Libra, dated 1034 AH / 1625 CE. The museum identifies Agra as its place of production.

title: Massachusetts Shilling
creator: John Hull and Robert Sanderson
caption: A silver shilling from Boston, Massachusetts, dated 1652. The museum attributes its fabrication to John Hull and Robert Sanderson.

title: Coins of the Qianlong Reign
creator: China, Qing dynasty
caption: A string of copper coins with square central holes. The museum places them in the Qianlong reign, 1736–95.

title: Four Mon Kan'ei Tsūhō Coin
creator: Japan, Edo period
caption: A copper four-mon coin from Edo-period Japan. The museum dates this example to 1768–1868.

title: Banknote Motif: Fifty
creator: Associated with Cyrus Durand
caption: An engraved proof places the number 50 within a lace-like rondel of lathe-work ornament. The museum associates the design with Cyrus Durand.
sourceNote: Museum catalogue title: Banknote motif: the number 50 against an ornamental lathe work rondel resembling lace

title: Banknote Motif: Six-Lobed Ornaments
creator: Associated with Cyrus Durand
medium: Engraving, printed in green ink; proof
caption: Two six-lobed lathe-work ornaments appear in this banknote-design proof. The engraving is printed in green ink and is associated with Cyrus Durand.
sourceNote: Museum catalogue title: Banknote motif: two six-lobed lathe work ornaments

title: Design for Banknote
creator: Robert William Hume
medium: Pen and ink, brush and wash, graphite
caption: Hume developed this banknote design in pen and ink, brush and wash, and graphite. Its ornate border surrounds an open field and the denomination five.

title: Design for Banknote or Certificate
creator: Robert William Hume
caption: A design for a banknote or certificate, drawn in pen and ink, graphite, and watercolor. The museum dates Hume’s sheet to 1830–1900.

title: Tenpō Tsūhō Coin
creator: Japan, Edo period
caption: A copper Tenpō Tsūhō coin from Edo-period Japan. The museum dates this example to 1835–68.

title: Victoria and Una: Five Pound Piece
creator: William Wyon
caption: William Wyon’s gold five-pound piece pairs Victoria with Una. It was made for presentation and collectors rather than circulation.
sourceNote: Museum catalogue title: Five Pound Piece: Victoria (obverse); Una (reverse)

title: Edward VII: Five Pound Piece
creator: George Edward de Saulles; after Benedetto Pistrucci
caption: A gold five-pound piece of 1902 pairs Edward VII with St. George and the dragon. The museum credits George Edward de Saulles and a design after Benedetto Pistrucci.
sourceNote: Museum catalogue title: Five Pound Piece: Edward VII (obverse); St. George and the Dragon (reverse)
